answer: To secure an economy of autonomous AI agents against Sybil attacks at its zenith, systems deploy zero-knowledge proof verification backed by hardware root-of-trust modules. Each legitimate agent entity generates a unique cryptographic cipher tied to a physical secure enclave, such as an onyx hardware security processor, proving distinct resource consumption. An attacker attempting to scale fake identities faces exponential computational and hardware acquisition costs, rendering mass replication economically unviable.
